title: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)

sections.label: Medium-Term Fiscal Projections Paper
sections.summary: The February 2023 Occasional Paper projects total revenue shrinking as a share of GDP to FY2030 while spending rises above 20% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in the Ministry’s Occasional Paper on Medium-Term Fiscal Projections dated February 2023, our total revenue is projected to shrink as a percentage of GDP up to FY2030, whereas Government spending is expected to increase from 18% of GDP today to more than 20% of GDP by FY2030.

sections.label: GST registration threshold
sections.summary: The GST registration threshold of $1 million has been in place since 1994.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, the registration threshold of $1 million for the Goods and Services Tax (GST) has been in place since 1994.

sections.label: GST threshold and income tax
sections.summary: The question asks what factors the Ministry considers on the $1 million GST threshold and why it has not raised it amid inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share the factors that it considers with regard to the appropriateness of the $1 million registration threshold for GST and why it has not been minded to raise this threshold, particularly in view of inflation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, the chargeable income tax for the first $20,000 of one's personal income is 0%.

sections.label: Qualifying IP and tax incentive
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Minister would broaden qualifying IP for corporate tax and enhance the IP development tax incentive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister consider broadening the definition of qualifying IP for corporate tax purposes and enhance the IP development tax incentive to spearhead our overall innovation drive?

sections.label: Other Taxes B90
sections.summary: The question asks which taxes fall under Other Taxes, account code B90, which rose from $6.3 billion to $8.44 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What are the taxes lumped together under “Other Taxes”, account code B90?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This item has increased from an estimate of $6.3 billion to a revised estimate of $8.44 billion.

sections.label: Merdeka Generation Fund figures
sections.summary: The passage states the Government set aside $7.5 billion for the package against a projected $8.2 billion cost, and cites the Merdeka Generation Fund figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As usual, the Government has set aside money from the current-year Budget to fund the full cost of the package upfront.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This time, the Government has set aside $7.5 billion and the projected cost of the package is $8.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Back when the Merdeka Generation Fund was set up in May 2019, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong told the House that the Government would set aside $6.1 billion and that the projected cost of the Package is over $8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But on page 78 of the Government Financial Statements released in July 2023, there is now a note that says, “The estimated liabilities under the Merdeka Generation Fund as at 31 March 2023 are $6,021,419,859.64.” Even after adding the total net drawdown of about $400 million since 2019, the total cost of the Package now does not seem to add up to $8 billion.

sections.label: Budget allocations and funds
sections.summary: This year's Budget allocates $20.4 billion, with other funds including the $5 billion Future Energy Fund, $6 billion GST Voucher Fund and $2 billion Edusave top-up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The allocation in this year’s Budget is $20.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Other funds include the $5 billion Future Energy Fund to invest in critical infrastructures to catalyse the move to low-carbon electricity; the GST Voucher Fund of $6 billion; and the $2 billion top-up of the Edusave Endowment Fund to recognise and encourage our students to develop competencies, such as adaptive and inventive thinking, communication skills and civic literacy, that will prepare them better and be future-ready.

sections.label: SME-lite tender system
sections.summary: The SME-lite tender system was introduced in late 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The introduction of the SME-lite tender system in late 2023 is noteworthy.

sections.label: SME procurement and payments
sections.summary: The Government paid e-invoices below $5,000 before the 30-day credit period, and MOF was asked about Tender Lite, SME procurement burden, inclusiveness and payment disbursement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On payments, I note that the Government has fulfilled payments on e-invoices below $5,000 well before the 30-day credit period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, SMEs wonder if the invoicing and progressive payment process for larger contracts can be further simplified, such as in the verification of work completion and, especially when variation orders are involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand MOF had announced the Tender Lite procurement category in last year’s Budget to ease the Government tender journey for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On this note, can MOF: (a) update on the progress and effectiveness of Tender Lite’s implementation; (b) share if there are plans to further ease the administrative burden on SMEs during the Government’s procurement process, such as through further digitisation and automation; (c) consider improving inclusiveness of smaller SMEs and startups so that they can participate in Government procurement, such as by adjusting the requirements to prefer homegrown enterprises or MNCs that partner with them, so that our local businesses can also participate in the supply chain; and (d) share how the Government can improve the disbursement of payments and grants to be timelier and more frictionless to help SMEs ease their cash flow challenges?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: In the drive to meet the targets and as a large purchaser of goods and services, public sector procurement plays a key role in catalysing the transition to green and achieving Singapore’s ambitious net-zero emission goals by 2030 and, subsequently, 2050.

sections.label: Philanthropic climate mitigation funding
sections.summary: Less than 2% of philanthropic dollars are estimated to be allocated towards climate mitigation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Currently, it is estimated that less than 2% of the philanthropic dollars are allocated towards climate mitigation.

sections.label: Blended finance in Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore has made consistent efforts to grow blended finance, including through MAS' Financing Asia's Transition Partnership.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore has made consistent efforts to grow blended finance, for example, through the MAS’ Financing Asia’s Transition Partnership.

sections.label: Zero Gap fund
sections.summary: The Zero Gap fund, established by the Rockefeller Foundation and the MacArthur Foundation, committed $30 million, mobilising over $795 million in private capital as of 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: A global example is the Zero Gap fund established by the Rockefeller Foundation and the MacArthur Foundation, which committed $30 million in catalytic investments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: As of 2022, this sum has, in turn, mobilised more than $795 million in private capital for projects aimed at achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.

sections.label: Tax deduction for overseas donations
sections.summary: The 100% tax deduction offered should catalyse increased cash donations to approved overseas emergency humanitarian assistance causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The 100% tax deduction offered should catalyse increased cash donations to approve overseas emergency humanitarian assistance causes.

sections.label: Tender Lite and simpler conditions
sections.summary: MOF will cut contract conditions by about 20%, remove Security Deposits and Liquidated Damages by default, and launch Tender Lite from April 2024 for tenders up to $1 million.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: First, MOF will cut the number of contract conditions by about 20% by streamlining the clauses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MOF will remove the requirements for Security Deposits and Liquidated Damages by default for Tender Lite.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MOF will be launching Tender Lite from April 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Tender Lite will cover tenders up to $1 million for general goods and services.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: With quotations and Tender Lite, around 90% of Government contracts will be subject to simpler procurement conditions which will benefit our SMEs.

sections.label: Invoices paid ahead of credit terms
sections.summary: For September 2020 to January 2022, 97% of invoices below $5,000 were paid ahead of their credit terms.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Instead, it should be, "For the period of September 2020 to January 2022, 97% of invoices below $5,000 were paid ahead of their credit terms.

sections.label: Climate reporting requirements for companies
sections.summary: From FY2025 listed companies must prepare climate reporting based on local standards, and from FY2027 large non-listed companies must provide climate-related disclosures and external limited assurance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: From FY2025, all listed companies will have to prepare climate reporting based on local prescribed reporting standards, which are aligned to those of the International Sustainability Standards Board.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: From FY2027, non-listed companies with annual revenue of at least $1 billion and total assets of at least $500 million will be required to provide climate-related disclosures.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Listed companies and large non-listed companies, as defined above, are also required to obtain external limited assurance on Scope 1 and Scope 2 Greenhouse Gas emissions two years after they start reporting, from FY2027 and FY2029 respectively.

sections.label: Scope 3 emissions disclosure
sections.summary: Listed companies will be required to disclose Scope 3 emissions from FY2026, a year after mandatory climate reporting.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Listed companies will be required to disclose Scope 3 emissions from FY2026, a year after mandatory climate reporting.

sections.label: Sustainability evaluation points for tenders
sections.summary: Starting from FY2024, up to 5% of evaluation points will be set aside for sustainability-related considerations for larger construction and ICT tenders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Starting from FY2024, we will set aside up to 5% of evaluation points for sustainability-related considerations, for larger construction and infocomm technology (ICT) tenders, which are in addition to the existing high standards that we require for our buildings and ICT equipment.

sections.label: Sustainability training and procurement
sections.summary: Government is developing sustainability training for public officers and targets including environmental sustainability in all procurement by 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Within the Government, we are also developing training programmes to strengthen public officers’ capabilities on sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We are on track to achieve our target to include environmental sustainability considerations in all Government procurement by 2028, but further progress also depends on industry readiness and international developments.

sections.label: Tender Lite from April
sections.summary: From April this year, Tender Lite will simplify terms for over 90% of government contracts, easing business participation in tenders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Starting from April this year, we will implement Tender Lite, simplifying terms for over 90% of government contracts and making it easier for businesses to participate in government tenders.

sections.label: Personal income tax exemption threshold
sections.summary: The $20,000 exemption threshold is higher than Malaysia, the UK and Australia, and around 40% of workers pay no income tax.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: On the personal income tax exemption threshold, our $20,000 exemption threshold is higher than jurisdictions like Malaysia, the UK and Australia, where thresholds range from around S$1,500 to S$16,000.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The threshold, taken together with our progressive tax rates, tax reliefs and rebates, results in around 40% of all workers not having to pay any income tax.

sections.label: GST registration threshold origin
sections.summary: The current $1 million GST registration threshold was put in place when the GST system was introduced in 1994.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: As for the GST registration threshold, the current threshold of $1 million was put in place when the GST system was introduced in 1994.

sections.label: GST threshold remains relevant
sections.summary: The $1 million threshold remains relevant today, as around 90% of businesses continue to be exempted from GST registration.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The $1 million threshold remains relevant today, as around 90% of businesses continue to be exempted from GST registration.

sections.label: FDWLR lapse announcement
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced in Budget 2023 that the FDWLR would lapse with effect from the Year of Assessment 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced in Budget 2023 that the FDWLR would lapse with effect from the Year of Assessment 2025.

sections.label: Charity donations matched since 2020
sections.summary: The programme has supported 480 charities and matched almost $200 million in donations since 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The programme has supported 480 charities and matched almost $200 million in donations since 2020.

sections.label: Future-Ready Society Impact Fund launch
sections.summary: Tote Board, the Lee Kuan Yew Centre for Innovative Cities and the Institute of Policy Studies launched the Future-Ready Society Impact Fund and Knowledge Partnership last year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Tote Board, together with the Lee Kuan Yew Centre for Innovative Cities and the Institute of Policy Studies, launched the Future-Ready Society Impact Fund and Knowledge Partnership last year to provide funding support for piloting innovative, evidence-based solutions that can enhance the resilience of our social ecosystem.

sections.label: Government expenditure share of GDP
sections.summary: Government expenditure is about 18% of GDP, among the lowest across advanced economies, while Singapore ranks highly on many indices.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Today, our Government expenditure as a share of GDP is about 18%, which is among the lowest across advanced economies; yet at the same time, we are ranked highly on many economic and social indices.

sections.label: FY 2023 ministry budget cut
sections.summary: In FY 2023, the Government cut all Ministries' and Organs of State budgets by 1% and channelled the funds to new and emerging priorities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For instance, in FY 2023, the Government implemented a 1% cut to the budgets of all Ministries and Organs of State and channelled the funds towards new and emerging priorities.

sections.label: Cost avoidance on infrastructure projects
sections.summary: MOF achieved total cost avoidance of around $1.6 billion, or 7.6% of capital costs, on large infrastructure projects submitted in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Of the large infrastructure projects submitted for approval in 2023, MOF was able to achieve total cost avoidance of around $1.6 billion, or 7.6% of projects' capital costs, by working with agencies to explore more cost-effective solutions and alternatives, and size the scope and budget of the projects judiciously.

sections.label: Cross-Island Line tunnel cost avoidance
sections.summary: For Cross-Island Line phase 2, twin-bore tunnels instead of single-bore tunnels for selected stretches is expected to avoid about $310 million in costs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For phase 2 development of the Cross-Island Line, it was assessed that twin-bore tunnels instead of single-bore tunnels could be used for selected stretches.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This is expected to achieve cost avoidance of approximately $310 million.

sections.label: Singapore Chartered Accountant Qualification enhancement
sections.summary: Enhancing the SCAQ will create more opportunities for local polytechnic graduates to become professional accountants.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: One key initiative is the enhancement of the Singapore Chartered Accountant Qualification (SCAQ), which will create more opportunities for local polytechnic graduates to become professional accountants.

sections.label: ASEAN pilot implementation timeline
sections.summary: A six-month pilot has commenced with six ASEAN member states, with implementation aimed for the third quarter of 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: A six-month pilot has commenced with six ASEAN member states and we aim to implement the arrangement in the third quarter of 2024.

sections.label: MG Fund injection amount
sections.summary: In 2019, more than $8 billion was projected for MG seniors, but only $6.1 billion was injected because the fund grows yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Back in 2019, we projected that we would need more than $8 billion in total to meet our commitments to all MG seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, to meet this spending, we did not have to set aside the entire $8 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We needed to inject only $6.1 billion into the MG Fund because every year, the fund grows from investment and interest income.

sections.label: Remaining MG liabilities estimate
sections.summary: After payouts over four years, the estimated amount needed to meet remaining liabilities is $6 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Taking into account that we have already met some of our commitments from paying out over the last four years, the estimated amount needed to meet remaining liabilities is $6 billion.

sections.label: Levy, land sales, property tax receipts
sections.summary: Foreign Worker Levy is projected at about $6.5 billion for FY2023 and $6.8 billion for FY2024, with higher land sales receipts expected in FY2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On Foreign Worker Levy, the total levy collected is projected to be around $6.5 billion for FY2023 and around $6.8 billion for FY2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On land sales proceeds, the receipts fluctuate based on the projected number and value of land sales each year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These are driven by our physical planning needs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are estimating higher receipts in FY2024 because we expect more higher-value land sales in the coming year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On property taxes, because Mr Leong asked why there is a significant increase for property taxes of private properties in 2024 despite the revision of the taxable Annual Value (AV) bands, we would like to clarify that the revisions in the AV bands will only take effect from 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: I should also point out that the $753 million figure was actually the change in property tax collections for all privately-owned properties, not just private residential properties.

sections.label: Budget Book detail comparison
sections.summary: The Budget Book has a comparable amount of detail to jurisdictions like Hong Kong and India.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As it stands, our Budget Book has a comparable amount of detail to jurisdictions like Hong Kong and India.

sections.label: FY2022 Financial Statements reference
sections.summary: Mr Leong can refer to the FY2022 Financial Statements, available publicly, for the latest figures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Leong can refer to the FY2022 Financial Statements available publicly for the latest figures.

sections.label: Development project spending in Budget Book
sections.summary: Spending on all development projects is in the Budget Book, including projects over $1 billion like Woodlands Health Campus and Deep Tunnel Sewerage System Phase 2.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The spending on all development projects is available in the Budget Book.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This includes ongoing projects with total project costs exceeding $1 billion, such as the Woodlands Health Campus and Phase 2 of the Deep Tunnel Sewerage System.

sections.label: Temasek capital injections figures
sections.summary: MOF provided figures for 20 years up to March 2022, and since then capital injections into Temasek are similar to the historical average.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: MOF provided him the figures for 20 years up to March 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Since then, capital injections into Temasek are similar to the average annual historical capital injections mentioned in our earlier PQ reply.

sections.label: Other Taxes estimated at $8.86 billion
sections.summary: The Budget Book estimates Other Taxes, including Foreign Worker Levy, Water Conservation Tax, Land Betterment Charge and Annual Tonnage Tax, at $8.86 billion, 0.9% higher than Revised FY2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: When you look at the Budget Book, Sir, what it says is that Other Taxes, which include the Foreign Worker Levy, Water Conservation Tax, Land Betterment Charge and Annual Tonnage Tax, are estimated to be $8.86 billion, which is $77.7 million or 0.9% higher than the Revised FY2023.

sections.label: Lumped $8.44 billion amount
sections.summary: The $8.44 billion comprising Foreign Worker Levy, Water Conservation Tax and Land Betterment Charge is lumped into one amount with no further breakdown in the Budget Book.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Chairman, yes, I thank the Minister for the further clarification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, now we have confirmed basically that this big item of $8.44 billion, which consists of the Foreign Worker Levy, Water Conservation Tax, Land Betterment Charge, it is all lumped up into one very big amount and there is no further breakdown on it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, all I am confirming is that in the Budget Book that is how it is presented.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As to whether there is any further detailed breakdown elsewhere, I would have to check.

sections.label: Information on SINGA Bill projects
sections.summary: An integrated view of budgeting is needed, and Parliament is asked for more information on projects under the SINGA Bill and SINGA financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So I think we need actually an integrated view of this whole budgeting process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: And the third thing we want to know is that since we have already passed the SINGA Bill and the big infrastructure projects are under this SINGA Bill and the SINGA Bill is also reported in the Budget – in terms of the capitalised costs and all that – so can Parliament have more information on the projects that are inside the SINGA Bill, that are under the SINGA financing?

sections.label: Other Taxes budget detail
sections.summary: The Government says its Budget already gives much detail on Other Taxes, comparable to what other countries provide.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For his first clarification, he asked whether or not for the medium-term — actually no, before he got on to that, he was asking whether or not we could give even more granular detail on the "Other Taxes".

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I come back to the reply that I made earlier, which is that the Government's Budget is a huge budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And already, as you can see from the Budget Book, a lot of detail is already given.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, there is a question of how much do you actually need for the purposes of the Budget and what we have given, as I said, is the same as what other countries give.

sections.label: Projections use standard methods
sections.summary: The speaker says projections are driven by long-term drivers and use the same standards as other countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Now again, I come back to this – which is that firstly, they are driven by long-term drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But at the end of the day, when we put out our projections – it is the same kind of standards that other countries use.

sections.label: Funding from funds or Budget
sections.summary: Spending is generally funded through the annual Budget, while funds are used for specific known needs including large commitments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But if he was asking how we decide whether our funding for specific purposes comes from the funds or the annual Budgets, is that the thrust of the question?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, generally we fund our spending through the annual Budget and we use funds for specific needs, which we know will come up, including large commitments.
